adversarial_finding: R2 0.477 is a between-band separation statistic, not within-band prediction. 58.4% of label variance is between three coarse eps bands (ss_between 12595/ss_total 21575), so R2=0.477 is BELOW the between-band share, i.e. all apparent skill is band separation and within-band skill is negative in 2 of 3 bands. The headline is also movable by one molecule and is computed on a 221-molecule set that silently dropped the 36 highest-eps molecules.
evidence_detail: Reproduced exactly (independent ridge, same nested-LOO): n=221, MAE 3.2999, R2 0.4770, RMSE 7.145, bias 0.008, rho 0.768; constant baseline 5.0932 confirmed. Bands (eps<5 / 5-20 / >20): n=106/100/15. Within LOW band model MAE 2.472 vs band-constant 0.894 (R2_within -12.89, bias +1.32); MID 2.543 vs 2.796 (R2_within +0.20, rho 0.62); HIGH 14.199 vs 12.160 (R2_within -0.16, bias -14.20). So the model is worse than 'say the band mean' in 2 of 3 bands and by 2.8x in the band holding 48% of the molecules. Oracle 3-band-mean predictor alone: MAE 2.519, R2 0.584 (better than the 20-feature model). Single-molecule influence: drop eps=114.9 -> R2 0.603, MAE 2.633; winsorise at 95% (11 capped) -> R2 0.637, MAE 2.367. Subsets: eps>=20 (n=15) R2 -0.162, MAE 14.20; eps>=10 (n=36) R2 0.177, MAE 7.56; eps<5 (n=103) R2 -14.43; halocarbon (n=67) R2 -2.61; non-halocarbon (n=154) R2 0.502. Log target R2 0.721. MAE 3.30 = 64% of median eps (5.13) and 43% of mean eps (7.61). The 36 excluded molecules are systematically high-eps (mean 16.68 vs 7.61; 27.8% vs 6.8% with eps>=20; Mann-Whitney p=0.068). 'Predicts liquid eps well' is not supported by these numbers; the reproduced numbers are.

adversarial_finding: The 2-vs-15 feature comparison is unfair as constructed and the '2 features' attribution is wrong. The 15 structural columns include a constant column (formal_charge), an exact duplicate pair (molar_volume_m3_mol vs molecular_volume_A3, r=0.9999999996) and a fingerprint-bit count, i.e. 12 real features; ridge on 15 is diluted below its own best 2-column subset. The mu2/Vm+alpha/Vm pair is really one working feature plus one inert one, and an unconstrained pair {dipole^2, 1/Vm} beats it.
evidence_detail: Reproduced: Xn 2 features MAE 4.1030 R2 0.2961; X0 15 features MAE 4.3992 R2 0.0958; pairable 16-feature combination X0+mu2Vm R2 0.3714. Column defects: formal_charge constant (1 unique value), corr(molar_volume, molecular_volume)=0.9999999996, morgan2_nbits vs heavy_atom r=0.60, mw vs heavy_atom r=0.74. Fair structural baselines: all C(15,2)=105 pairs searched; best pair tpsa_A2+molecular_volume_A3 R2 0.1955 MAE 4.211, heavy_atom+tpsa R2 0.1924; cleaned 13-column X0 R2 0.1157 (vs 0.0958 with the junk columns). Single features: mu2/Vm R2 0.2360 MAE 3.935 (better MAE than the 2-feature block); 1/molar_volume R2 0.2439 MAE 4.678; alpha_over_Vm R2 0.0147 rho -0.064 (worse than nothing); alpha_over_Vm added to mu2/Vm worsens MAE 3.935->4.103 (paired delta 0.168, 95% CI -0.13..0.47, worse in 87% of bootstrap resamples). Unconstrained {dipole^2, 1/Vm}: 2 features, R2 0.3625 MAE 4.182, i.e. better than the Kirkwood product form. Honest claim: 'mu2/Vm alone beats the 12 real structural descriptors'; not '2 features, one of them alpha/Vm, beat 15'.

adversarial_finding: Attacked with paired bootstrap on the same 221 molecules: dipole-only and the 3-feature electronic block are statistically indistinguishable in MAE, and neither polarisability nor the HOMO-LUMO gap adds anything conditional on dipole. The claim survives; only its R2 framing needs care (the block's R2 0.191 vs 0.114 is a shrinkage/outlier effect, not better typical accuracy).
evidence_detail: Reproduced: dipole_only MAE 4.3470 R2 0.1137 rho 0.692; electronic_3 MAE 4.3265 R2 0.1908 rho 0.778; alpha_only R2 0.0676 MAE 4.950; gap_only R2 0.0247 MAE 4.931; dipole+alpha MAE 4.4217 (worse than dipole alone); dipole+gap MAE 4.3377. Paired bootstrap (per-molecule |err|): dipole vs electronic_3 delta 0.0204 (95% CI -0.281..+0.316), dipole better on 121/221; dipole vs dipole+gap delta 0.0092 (CI -0.032..+0.049); dipole vs dipole+alpha delta -0.0747 (CI -0.385..+0.225). Conditional on dipole+mu2/Vm: adding polarisability delta MAE -0.058 (worse), adding gap +0.006 (noise). alpha_over_Vm alone R2 0.0147, rho -0.064. Residual caveat for the write-up: report this on MAE/RMSE, because on R2 the block looks 68% better and that difference is produced by a handful of high-eps molecules. Note also that this result contradicts claim B's attribution of value to alpha/Vm; C is the correct one.

adversarial_finding: Both halves of the claim are broken. (i) '6/8 families beat the baseline' is a weak-strawman artefact: the e4 baseline is the global leave-one-family-out TRAIN mean, which is trivially far from any low-eps family mean, so almost any model that predicts 'low' beats it; 6/8 families have NEGATIVE R2 and only 2/8 beat an honest nested family-mean constant. (ii) The stated cause of the halocarbon failure ('lowest-eps family, eps barely varies with structure') is factually false: halocarbon is the 3rd-lowest family (mean 5.98 vs 2.55 for alkanes and 2.97 for aromatics), its eps spans 2.24-10.19 (CV 0.30) and is predictable in-family (LOO R2 0.51, MAE 0.85). The real failure is absolute-scale calibration: bias +3.10, predicted sd 8.05 vs true sd 1.79, and an oracle 2-parameter recalibration of the SAME predictions gives MAE 1.23, better than the 1.48 family constant - so the model carries cross-family signal.
evidence_detail: Reproduced e4 exactly (6/8, halocarbon MAE 6.7778 vs baseline 2.5306, R2 -18.4656). Halocarbon: n=67, eps mean 5.978, sd 1.794, min 2.238, max 10.190, IQR 2.445, CV 0.300, 22/67 below 5. Baselines on the same 67: global train mean 8.319 -> MAE 2.531 (published); oracle family mean -> 1.477; nested family mean -> 1.500; in-family 2-feature LOO (n_rotatable+n_halogen) -> 0.895; in-family 18-feature LOO -> 0.850 (R2 0.510). Transfer model: MAE 6.778, bias +3.103, prediction sd 8.05, Spearman 0.568, only 6/67 within 20% relative error (median relative error 119%), 50/67 over-predicted, lambda 10 (max of grid). Oracle mean-shift -> 5.508; oracle slope+intercept recalibration -> 1.233. Across 8 families: negative R2 in 6/8; vs nested family mean only 2/8 win (alcohol 4.845<5.835; ketone 2.965<3.697) while halocarbon 6.778>1.500, aromatic 4.647>0.949, other_neutral 2.249>0.951, ester 3.842>2.854, ether 3.373>2.618, amine 9.007>8.690. Family eps means: other_neutral 2.55, aromatic 2.97, ether 5.86, halocarbon 5.98, ester 6.83, alcohol 8.88, ketone 14.49, amine(nitro) 20.47. Mechanistic diagnosis (mine): halocarbon has mean dipole 3.45 D - essentially the same as ketones (3.48 D) - but mean eps 5.98 vs 14.49, i.e. it is the family where the model's dominant predictor (mu2/Vm) is least transferable; the lowest-eps family (alkanes, mu 0.19 D, eps 2.55) is well calibrated (bias -0.21), so low eps per se is not the driver. Family-level analysis is also chemically invalid: 14 of the 21 'amine' members are nitro compounds and 6 are nitrate esters (amine SMARTS catches nitro N), so the 'amine' row (mean eps 21.4) is a nitro/nitrate row; the readiness report claims the nitro family is empty while 14 nitro compounds are present mislabelled.

adversarial_finding: The 2.23 ratio reproduces and is robust to the Tanimoto threshold (2.23 at 0.5, 5.74 at 0.3, 2.46 at 0.7), so the number is not a post-hoc artefact of 0.5. But 'effective' is unsupported: the ratio is tail-driven (median-error ratio only 1.28), it is reversed in 2 of 8 families, vanishes in the 5-10 eps stratum, and the domain test throws away exactly the molecules screening needs (8 of the 15 eps>=20 molecules are out-of-domain, and in-domain eps>=20 MAE is still 10.58). The threshold is descriptive, never validated against a held-out calibration.
evidence_detail: Reproduced: 151 in / 70 out at 0.5, MAE in 2.6551, out 5.9179, ratio 2.2289. Threshold sweep (ratio, bootstrap CI): 0.30 -> 5.735 [1.42,13.61]; 0.40 -> 3.228; 0.45 -> 2.527; 0.50 -> 2.229 [1.32,3.59]; 0.60 -> 2.268; 0.70 -> 2.459 [1.72,3.59]; 0.80 -> 2.509. Median-error ratio at 0.5 is only 1.275 (1.930 in vs 2.461 out), i.e. typical error shifts by ~0.5 eps units while the mean ratio is inflated by a few large failures. eps-stratified ratios: [0,5) 1.637, [5,10) 1.078, [10,20) 2.126, [20,inf) 2.381. Within-family: halocarbon 0.886 and aromatic 0.985 (reversed), ether 2.92, alcohol 4.21. Excluding halocarbons: ratio 2.559. Confound check: out-of-domain molecules have higher eps (mean 9.92 vs 6.54) but partial Spearman(error, similarity | eps) = -0.261 vs raw -0.276, so similarity carries some independent signal. In-domain composition is dominated by near-duplicate homologous series (e.g. 48/67 halocarbons in-domain), which is why in-domain errors are low. In-domain MAE at eps>=20 is 10.578, so being 'in domain' does not make a prediction usable. No decision-level evidence (e.g. that gating on 0.5 improves top-k selection) is provided.

adversarial_finding: p=0.0036 reproduces exactly, but it measures motif/family recognition, not eps screening. The model's top-10 is 9 nitro/nitrate compounds + acetic acid; a family-matched null (9 draws from the same family + 1 acid) gives p=0.249, i.e. within the family it is random. Three trivial one-descriptor rankers beat the 20-feature model on the same metric, and its #1 pick is the pool's 177th-best molecule. Only 42.4% of headroom is captured, 4/10 of the true top-10, 18% of the top 20%. 'Significantly better than random' is a bar so low that a single physical descriptor clears it far more convincingly.
evidence_detail: Reproduced: k=10, oracle 39.09, model 20.9661, pool mean 7.6095, regret 18.1239; my independent MC (400k draws) p=0.003605. Headroom captured (20.9661-7.6095)/(39.09-7.6095)=42.4%. Oracle overlap 4/10; recall of top-10% 8/22=36%; of top-20% 8/44=18%; NDCG@10 0.366. True ranks of the model's picks: 177,17,5,9,18,22,90,4,3,16. #1 pick tetranitromethane eps=2.521 predicted 24.153 (rank 177/221); the two most valuable molecules are missed: eps=114.9 rank 19, glycerol eps=41.17 rank 24. Family-matched null: model top-10 = 9 'amine'(=nitro/nitrate) + 1 acid; drawing 9 from that family + 1 acid gives mean 18.86 and p=0.249. Single-descriptor top-10 on the same pool: mu2/Vm 26.875 (p=2.0e-5), 1/MW 26.071 (p=4.5e-5), 1/molar_volume 25.558 (p=6.5e-5), n_halogen ascending 21.768 (p=1.9e-3, 9/10 identical to the model's picks), tpsa 19.62 (p=8.5e-3), dipole 16.60 (p=0.032). Dropping the 1/2/3/5 highest-eps molecules: p<=3e-6 and headroom captured rises to 60%/65%/66%/65%, so p is NOT driven by the extreme labels (the 42.4% headroom number is). k-sensitivity: k=5 model 19.184, headroom 26.7%, p=0.0245; k=15 22.511, headroom 56.7%. Regional note: the top-10 selection is essentially 'not a halocarbon, high nitrate content', which is why the pool's 67 halocarbons never appear.

adversarial_finding: 30/36 reproduces, but only under the stated 10% OR rule, and it is driven almost entirely by the max-min spread statistic (30/30 flagged by spread; only 16 by the single-conformer-vs-Boltzmann deviation, whose median is just 7.9%). The fraction is 36/36 (100%) at a 5% threshold and 23/36 (64%) at 20%, so the headline number is threshold-arbitrary. Scope is also narrower than the wording: the sample is 40 molecules purposefully chosen as the most flexible (n_rot>=6), which is 48/257 molecules = 18.7% of the dataset; 30/36 must not be read as a dataset-wide rate.
evidence_detail: Reproduced from conformer_ensemble_b100.csv: 40 rows, 36 polar (Boltzmann dipole >= 0.30), 3 non-polar, 1 not analysed; OR-rule at 10% flags 30/36 = 83.3% (spread criterion 30, deviation criterion 16, both 16). Threshold sweep (OR rule on the 36): 2% 36/36; 5% 36/36 (100%); 10% 30/36 (83%); 15% 23/36 (64%); 20% 23/36 (64%); 30% 21/36 (58%); 50% 10/36 (28%). Distribution: median relative spread 0.329, median single-vs-Boltzmann deviation 0.079, max spread 2.64. Scope: sample n_rot min 6, median 10; dataset has 48/257 (18.7%) with n_rot>=6 and the 40 sampled are 83% of them. Consequence for the model (my calculation): at the median mu2/Vm, a 2x-relative-spread dipole uncertainty maps to an eps shift of ~1.62 using the 33% spread, but only ~0.39 using the 7.9% typical single-vs-Boltzmann deviation, against a model MAE of 3.30. So the qualitative conclusion (single conformer is not a reliable Boltzmann dipole for flexible polar molecules) stands and is if anything stronger at 5%; the 83% figure should be reported as a range (64-100%) with its flexibility scope.

adversarial_finding: The count gates are met honestly: 257 unique InChIKeys, every label traceable to a ledger row with a matching temperature, all measurements 293.15-303.15 K (max 5 K from 298.15, which is worth only ~2.3% in eps), and the non-static-frequency risk is documented and small (only one label comes from a >0 MHz measurement, at 0.05 MHz; the 20 core rows at up to 3 MHz differ from static values by ~0.1%). Unknown-melting-point molecules were excluded rather than defaulted, which is the honest choice. What is not supported is 'the dataset supports a 100+ molecule study' in the inferential sense: 226/257 records come from one compilation with only 18 independently corroborated, only 15 molecules have eps>=20, 14% of the 257 silently exit the 221-molecule analysis set (and they are the high-eps ones), and the family stratification is partly fictional (the 'amine' family is 14 nitro + 6 nitrate + 7 amine/aniline).
evidence_detail: Gate reconciliation: admission gate 306 qualified / 242 with xTB; freeze manifest 257 qualified / 257 xTB (240 reused + 17 newly computed); modelling set 257; common evaluation set 221. Label provenance: 257/257 labels match a ledger row exactly in both eps and T (no interpolation, no untraceable label). Temperature: T in [293.15, 303.15], 81 at 298.15, 92 within 2 K, max |T-298.15| = 5.0 K; empirical median fractional d eps/dT = -0.462%/K (30 molecules with T series) -> 5 K = 2.3% = 0.21 eps units, negligible against MAE 3.30. Frequency: 238 NBS-514 rows carry no per-measurement frequency (documented source-level static definition, 127 footnote rows with 360-500 MHz were excluded at transcription); 20 ThermoML rows report 0.01-3 MHz (nitrobenzene 3 MHz 34.78 vs static label 34.82 = 0.1%); only 1 label (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) is sourced from a non-zero-frequency row (0.05 MHz). Label repeatability: 31 molecules have >=2 measurements within 10 K of 298: median relative range 2.5%, p90 10.3%, 13% above 10%. Attrition: the 36 molecules dropped for missing polarizability have mean eps 16.68 (median 6.83, max 178.47) vs 7.61 for the 221, and 27.8% vs 6.8% are eps>=20 (Mann-Whitney p=0.068). Independence: 226 Q2 from NBS 514, 31 Q1, 18 independently corroborated. Family balance: 8 families with >=10 members, 4 with <10 (carboxylic 4, nitrile 3, carbonate 2, phosphate 1); 'amine' = 14 nitro + 6 nitrate + 7 amine/aniline. Effective high-eps support is 15 molecules, which is why H4 is INSUFFICIENT_POWER.
